intended_object: For a face τ of a cone σ, the finite set of rays (one-dimensional faces) of σ that lie in τ. Equivalently, the rays of τ viewed as rays of σ, i.e. the subset τ(1) ⊆ σ(1) of toric geometry (Fulton §1.2, Cox–Little–Schenck §1.2). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition takes the range of `faceEmbedding hτ : ToricRay τ ↪ ToricRay σ`. This map sends each ray of τ to itself, seen as a ray of σ: a face of a face is a face, and the dimension condition does not involve the ambient cone. The range is finite because `finite_of_fg` gives finitely many rays for a finitely generated τ, so it is turned into a `Finset` with `Set.Finite.toFinset`.

The library proves `mem_faceFinset`: ρ belongs to the set exactly when ρ ≤ τ. This matches the intended set of rays of σ contained in τ, and the rays of τ are exactly those rays (`range_faceEmbedding`).

The hypothesis `τ.FG` is only there to get finiteness, so it is the right condition for a `Finset` version. Working over ℝ is the convention of the whole toric library, and the underlying `ToricRay` notion is defined over ℝ, so this is not a separate narrowness issue for this definition. Mathlib has no notion of the rays of a pointed cone, or of the rays inside a face, to compare against.
